questions.statement: Which word in English names the part of the body where you think when you study?
questions.context: In a school nurse's office in Armenia, a boy points to his forehead because he feels hot.

options.text: Head.
options.feedback: The head includes the brain, where you think and which controls the body.

options.text: Knee.
options.feedback: The knee is a joint in the leg used for walking, not for thinking.

options.text: Wrist.
options.feedback: The wrist connects the hand to the arm, not used for thinking.

options.text: Ankle.
options.feedback: The ankle is a joint in the leg, not used for thinking.

questions.explanation: Identifying basic external body parts by their function in English (head, knee, wrist, ankle).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why does Camila have a stomach ache?
questions.context: Read: "Camila has a stomach ache because she ate too much candy yesterday."

options.text: Because she ate too much candy yesterday.
options.feedback: The text directly states that eating too much candy caused the stomach ache.

options.text: Because she drank too much water.
options.feedback: Drinking water is not mentioned as a cause of her stomach ache.

options.text: Because she ran a lot in P.E. class.
options.feedback: Physical activity is not mentioned in the passage.

options.text: Because she slept too many hours.
options.feedback: Sleeping is not stated as the cause of her stomach ache.

questions.explanation: Inferring the cause of a health problem from a short descriptive text in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports how the boy feels using the verb "have"?
questions.context: A doctor asks: "How do you feel today?" A boy answers: "I have a headache and a sore throat."

options.text: He has a headache and a sore throat.
options.feedback: "Has" agrees with the third person singular subject "he".

options.text: He have a headache and a sore throat.
options.feedback: "Have" without -s is incorrect with "he" in Simple Present.

options.text: He having a headache and a sore throat.
options.feedback: "Having" is a gerund and needs an auxiliary verb in this construction.

options.text: He has a headaches and a sore throats.
options.feedback: "Headaches" and "sore throats" are unnecessary plurals here.

questions.explanation: Using the verb "have" with the third person singular to describe common health problems in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct imperative sentence that follows this advice.
questions.context: A nurse in Popayan says: "Wash your hands before lunch and after using the bathroom."

options.text: Wash your hands with soap and water.
options.feedback: The imperative base form "wash" gives a direct instruction to the listener.

options.text: You washes your hands with soap and water.
options.feedback: The imperative does not use a subject or the -s form of the verb.

options.text: Washing your hands with soap and water.
options.feedback: "Washing" is a gerund; imperatives use the base form of the verb.

options.text: To wash your hands with soap and water.
options.feedback: The infinitive form is not used as an imperative command.

questions.explanation: Giving simple health-related instructions using the imperative form in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly expresses a reason using "because"?
questions.context: A student writes about her day: "I feel tired because I did not sleep well last night."

options.text: She feels tired because she did not sleep well last night.
options.feedback: "Because" introduces a clear cause-effect relationship in the past simple.

options.text: She feels tired but she did not sleep well last night.
options.feedback: "But" expresses contrast, not the cause of feeling tired.

options.text: She feels tired so she did not sleep well last night.
options.feedback: The logic is reversed: not sleeping causes tiredness, not the other way around.

options.text: She feels tired because she sleep well last night.
options.feedback: "Sleep" should be in the past simple "slept" to match the past tense context.

questions.explanation: Using "because" to connect causes and effects when describing health and feelings in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the doctor recommend for Luis?
questions.context: Read: "Luis has a fever and a cough. The doctor says he should drink water, rest, and take medicine for three days."

options.text: Drink water, rest, and take medicine for three days.
options.feedback: The text lists these three actions as the doctor's advice.

options.text: Play soccer with friends every afternoon.
options.feedback: Physical activity is not part of the doctor's advice; rest is recommended instead.

options.text: Eat only candy and drink soda.
options.feedback: The doctor does not recommend candy or soda; he recommends water and rest.

options.text: Stay at school all night without sleeping.
options.feedback: Rest and sleep are recommended, the opposite of staying up all night.

questions.explanation: Identifying medical advice from a short descriptive paragraph in English.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which comparison correctly explains why Juan is healthier than Maria?
questions.context: Compare two children: "Maria has a toothache because she eats too much candy. Juan feels healthy because he brushes his teeth and eats fruits."

options.text: Juan brushes his teeth and eats fruits, while Maria eats too much candy.
options.feedback: Healthy habits (brushing, fruits) versus excessive candy explain their different health.

options.text: Juan also eats too much candy and never brushes his teeth.
options.feedback: The text says Juan has healthy habits, so this contradicts the passage.

options.text: Maria brushes her teeth every day and avoids candy.
options.feedback: The text says Maria has a toothache from candy, so this is incorrect.

options.text: Neither Maria nor Juan takes care of personal hygiene.
options.feedback: The text describes Juan as taking care of his hygiene.

questions.explanation: Comparing healthy and unhealthy habits described in English to draw conclusions about well-being.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the most important message of this paragraph?
questions.context: Read: 'Daily habits such as washing hands, brushing teeth, sleeping eight hours, and exercising help children stay healthy and prevent common illnesses at school.'

options.text: Healthy daily habits prevent illnesses and help children feel well at school.
options.feedback: The text links specific habits with staying healthy and preventing illnesses.

options.text: Children should not brush their teeth at all.
options.feedback: Brushing teeth is listed as a positive habit, so the paragraph does not oppose it.

options.text: Sleeping less than four hours is the best way to be healthy.
options.feedback: The text recommends eight hours of sleep, not less.

options.text: Exercising every day is harmful to the body.
options.feedback: The paragraph lists exercise among healthy habits, not as harmful.

questions.explanation: Evaluating the main message of a short expository paragraph about healthy daily habits.
questions.subject: ingles
